scores.visual_critic_note: Intentional Paul Tol palette with rank-colored nodes and a clean search/control bar creates a polished, readable tree, though the bottom half of the viewport is wasted whitespace at the default collapsed state.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Tree layout has no quantitative encoding violations—colors are categorical, node radii encode type not data, and descendant counts are computed dynamically—but node/link keys use name+depth strings instead of stable path-based IDs, creating a minor metamorphic robustness risk under data reorganization.
scores.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() call before new transitions in update(), so rapid clicks during the 500ms node expand/collapse animation can cause element snapping; all other traps are clean — search is debounced 200ms, pointer events prevent mouse-touch double-fire, no cross-view dispatch loops, and no scale closures in event listeners.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Progressive disclosure keeps the default view to ~15 visible nodes with a clean 6-color Tol palette, '+N' count badges on collapsed subtrees, and a search that auto-expands paths — cognitive load is well-managed even though the full tree has ~200 nodes.
